question: What do I bring to my first visit?
expectedResponse: Bring a photo ID and your insurance card, and arrive 15 minutes early to complete registration. Cites the Patient Intake policy.
actualResponse:
For your first visit, please:

- Arrive 15 minutes early to complete registration.
- Bring a photo ID and your insurance card.
- If your insurance has changed, bring your updated insurance card.
- If you are under 18, you must be accompanied by a parent or legal guardian.
- Complete intake forms in advance through the patient portal if possible, or you can complete them at check-in. These forms include medical history, current medications, allergies, and an emergency contact. [1]

This information is from the Patient Intake & Registration Policy. [1]

question: How do I get a copy of my records?
expectedResponse: Submit a written records request through the patient portal or front desk; records are provided within 10 business days and a small copying fee may apply. Cites the Privacy & Records policy.
actualResponse:
Per the Patient Privacy & Medical Records Policy, you can request a copy of your records by submitting a written records request through the patient portal or at the front desk. Records are provided within 10 business days, and a small copying fee may apply for large or printed requests. [1]

If you have questions about records or privacy, you can contact the Privacy Officer. [1]

question: What's the no-show fee?
expectedResponse: A late cancellation (under 24 hours) or no-show may incur a $35 fee. Cites the Scheduling policy.

question: How many PTO days do new full-time staff get, and when can I use them?
expectedResponse: 12 PTO days per year, accrued monthly from day one, but PTO cannot be used during the first 90 days. Cites the Staff Handbook.
actualResponse:
Per the Staff Handbook, new full-time staff receive 12 PTO days per year, accrued monthly. PTO starts accruing from your first day of employment, but it cannot be used during your first 90 days. After 3 years of employment, the PTO allowance increases to 18 days per year. [1]

question: My appointment is tomorrow but I need to cancel, will I be charged?
expectedResponse: Explains that at least 24 hours' notice is requested; cancelling under 24 hours before may incur a $35 late-cancellation fee. Suggests cancelling as early as possible via the reminder link, portal or phone. Cites the Scheduling policy.
actualResponse:

Since your appointment is tomorrow, whether a fee applies depends on whether you are still outside the 24-hour window. If you need to cancel, contact the clinic as soon as possible or use the reschedule option in your appointment reminder. [1]

If you have questions about your specific appointment, the policy directs patients to call the front desk at (555) 0100. [1]
